hints.text: Substituting gives $\frac{0}{0}$, which is a signal — not an answer. Factor the top.
$x^2 - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3)$, so the $(x - 3)$ on top cancels the one on the bottom.
What is left is $x + 3$, and at $x = 3$ that is $6$.

explanation: Substituting $x = 3$ gives $\frac{0}{0}$ — that means "keep working", not "no answer".
Factor the top as a difference of squares: $(x - 3)(x + 3)$.
Cancel the shared $(x - 3)$, leaving $x + 3$ everywhere except at the hole.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sneak up with a table
steps: Both sides squeeze toward 6 — the table agrees with the cancelling.

alternativeExplanations.title: What the graph really looks like
steps: After cancelling, the picture is just the straight line y = x + 3.
The only difference is a tiny open circle punched out at x = 3.
The line passes through height 6 there, so the limit is 6 — the hole changes nothing about where you are headed.
